name: Nouns
description: Words that name people, places, animals, things and ideas

topics.name: Common nouns
topics.description: A noun is a naming word. It can name a person, place, animal or thing. A common noun is an everyday name, such as boy, park or dog.
topics.example: The puppy sleeps beside the gate.

topics.name: Proper nouns
topics.description: A proper noun is the special name of a particular person, place, day, month or organisation. It starts with a capital letter.
topics.example: Sarah lives in Johannesburg.

topics.name: Collective nouns
topics.description: A collective noun is one word that names a group of people, animals or things.
topics.example: A flock of birds flew overhead.

topics.name: Abstract nouns
topics.description: An abstract noun names a feeling, idea or quality. You cannot hold or touch it, but you can feel it or understand it.
topics.example: Her kindness made everyone smile.

name: Pronouns
description: Words that stand in for names

topics.name: Personal pronouns
topics.description: A pronoun takes the place of a noun. Personal pronouns include I, you, he, she, it, we and they. They help us avoid repeating names.
topics.example: Lindiwe is reading. She likes stories.

topics.name: Possessive pronouns
topics.description: Possessive pronouns tell who something belongs to. Examples are mine, yours, his, hers, ours and theirs.
topics.example: This red jacket belongs to me. It is mine.

topics.name: Demonstrative pronouns
topics.description: These pronouns point to something. This and these usually point to things nearby. That and those usually point to things farther away.
topics.example: Those are the houses across the river.

topics.name: Interrogative pronouns
topics.description: Interrogative pronouns are question words used to ask about people or things. Who asks about a person. What asks about a thing. Which asks about a choice. Whose asks who owns something.
topics.example: Who left this note?

name: Verbs and tenses
description: Action words and when actions happen

topics.name: Action verbs
topics.description: A verb is a doing word or a being word. An action verb tells what someone or something does, such as jump, sing or write.
topics.example: The horse gallops across the field.

topics.name: Helping verbs
topics.description: A helping verb works with another verb. It helps show when an action happens. Common helping verbs are am, is, are, was, were, has, have and will.
topics.example: The girls are singing.

topics.name: Past tense
topics.description: Past tense tells us that an action already happened. Many verbs add -ed, but some change, such as eat becoming ate.
topics.example: Yesterday, I baked muffins.

topics.name: Present tense
topics.description: Present tense tells us what happens now or regularly. With he, she or it, we often add -s or -es to the verb.
topics.example: Every morning, Musa walks to school.

topics.name: Future tense
topics.description: Future tense tells us about something that will happen later. We often use will before the action verb.
topics.example: Next week, we will visit the zoo.

topics.description: An exclamation mark (!) can show strong feeling, excitement, surprise or a warning.
topics.example: Watch out!

topics.name: Apostrophes
topics.description: An apostrophe (’) can show ownership, as in the boy’s bag, or missing letters, as in can’t.
